Mr. Hari spends 36% of his income on food items and 25% of the remaining amount on clothes, medical and conveyance. He saves half of the remaining amount every month. If he saves ₹1,80,000 every year, then find his monthly income.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mr. Hari spends 36% of his income on food items.

He spends 25% of the remaining amount on clothes, medical, and conveyance.

He saves half of the remaining amount every month.

He saves ₹1,80,000 every year.

**Formula Used:**

Monthly Savings = Annual Savings / 12

Savings = 0.5 × Remaining Amount

Remaining Amount = Income - (Food + Clothes, Medical, and Conveyance)

**Calculation:**

Let Mr. Hari's monthly income be x.

Amount spent on food items = 36% of x = 0.36x

Remaining amount after spending on food = x - 0.36x = 0.64x

Amount spent on clothes, medical, and conveyance = 25% of remaining amount = 0.25 × 0.64x = 0.16x

Remaining amount after spending on food, clothes, medical, and conveyance = 0.64x - 0.16x = 0.48x

Savings = 0.5 × 0.48x = 0.24x

Monthly Savings = ₹1,80,000 / 12 = ₹15,000

So, 0.24x = ₹15,000

⇒ x = ₹15,000 / 0.24

⇒ x = ₹62,500

**Mr. Hari's monthly income is ₹62,500.**

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper claimed to have sold an item at ₹23/kg, which cost him ₹25/kg. However, by using faulty weights, he gave only 600 gm instead of 1 kg. What is his total percentage profit or loss?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price (SP) = ₹23/kg

Cost price (CP) = ₹25/kg

Weight given = 600 gm = 0.6 kg

**Formula Used:**

Profit or Loss% = ((SP - CP)/(CP)) times 100

**Calculation:**

Effective Selling Price for 1 kg = ₹23/0.6

Effective Selling Price for 1 kg = 23 × (5/3)

Effective Selling Price for 1 kg = ₹38.33

Profit = SP - CP

Profit = ₹38.33 - ₹25

Profit = ₹13.33

Profit% = ((₹13.33)/(₹25)) times 100

Profit% = ((1333)/(2500)) times 100

Profit% = 53.32%

**The total percentage profit is 53 ⅓%.**

questions.question: If LCM (27, n) = 54 and HCF (27, n) = 9, then the value of n is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula: Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

27 × n = 54 × 9

n = (54 ÷ 27) × 9

n = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (a) = 27

LCM(a, n) = 54

HCF(a, n) = 9

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = Least Common Multiple (LCM) × Highest Common Factor (HCF)

 Number 1: 27 Number 2: n × 
• = LCM: 54 HCF: 9 × 27 × n = 54 × 9 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 27 × n = 54 × 9

⇒ 27n = 486

⇒ n = 486 ÷ 27

⇒ n = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship for Two Numbers

For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. This rule only applies to exactly two numbers.

HCF of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime (e.g., 8 and 9), their HCF is 1 and their LCM is the product of the numbers.

Factor Property of HCF

The HCF of a set of numbers is always a factor of their LCM. In this case, 9 is a factor of 54 (9 × 6 = 54).

questions.question:
If θ is an acute angle, find the denominator D when

(cot θ - cosec θ)² = (1 - cos θ)/(D)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

(cot θ − cosec θ)² = (cosec θ − cot θ)²

⇒ [(1 / sin θ) − (cos θ / sin θ)]² = [(1 − cos θ) / sin θ]²

⇒ (1 − cos θ)² / sin² θ = (1 − cos θ)² / (1 − cos² θ)

⇒ (1 − cos θ)² / [(1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ)] = (1 − cos θ) / (1 + cos θ)

Comparing with (1 − cos θ) / D, we get D = 1 + cos θ.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + cos θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (cot θ − cosec θ)² = (1 − cos θ) / D

**Formula Used:** cot θ = Adjacent / Opposite; cosec θ = Hypotenuse / Opposite; cos θ = Adjacent / Hypotenuse

 Adjacent (b)
 Opposite (a)
 Hypotenuse (c)
 Right Triangle Ratios

Let Opposite = a, Adjacent = b, and Hypotenuse = c. Then a² + b² = c² ⇒ a² = c² − b².

⇒ cot θ = b/a and cosec θ = c/a

⇒ LHS = (b/a − c/a)² = [(b − c) / a]²

⇒ LHS = (b − c)² / a² = (c − b)² / (c² − b²)

⇒ LHS = (c − b)² / [(c − b)(c + b)] = (c − b) / (c + b)

⇒ LHS = [c(1 − b/c)] / [c(1 + b/c)] = (1 − cos θ) / (1 + cos θ)

⇒ (1 − cos θ) / (1 + cos θ) = (1 − cos θ) / D

⇒ D = 1 + cos θ

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + cos θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Identities

cosec θ = 1/sin θ; sec θ = 1/cos θ; cot θ = 1/tan θ = cos θ/sin θ.

Half-Angle Transformations

1 − cos θ = 2 sin²(θ/2) and 1 + cos θ = 2 cos²(θ/2). Thus, (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ) = tan²(θ/2).</p

questions.question: The cost price of a toy is ₹210. What should be its marked price so that, after a discount of 5%, the shopkeeper gains 90%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of the toy = ₹210

Discount = 5%

Gain = 90%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 + Gain%)

Marked Price (MP) = Selling Price (SP) / (1 - Discount%)

**Calculation:**

Selling Price (SP) = 210 × (1 + 90 / 100)

⇒ SP = 210 × 1.9 = 399

Marked Price (MP) = 399 / (1 - 5 / 100) = 399 / 0.95 = 420

**The marked price should be ₹420.**

questions.question: A ball of radius 10 cm is taken and a cylindrical hole of radius 1 cm is drilled through the centre. Which of the options listed below is the closest in value to the ratio of the total surface area of the hollowed out ball to the surface area of the original ball?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the original ball, R = 10 cm

Radius of the cylindrical hole, r = 1 cm

**Calculation:**

The surface area of a sphere = Aₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = 4πR²

Substituting R = 10 cm:

 Aₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = 4π (10)² = 400π cm²

Surface Area of the Hollowed-out Ball

When the cylindrical hole is drilled through the ball, we need to consider:

The surface area of the spherical part remains, i.e., 4πR²

The lateral surface area of the cylinder, given by A꜀yₗᵢₙdₑᵣ = 2πrh, where h is the height of the cylinder, equal to the diameter of the sphere, h = 2R = 20 cm.

The two circular areas at the ends of the drilled hole, each with an area of πr², which are subtracted from the spherical surface.

The Lateral Surface Area of the Cylinder

 A꜀yₗᵢₙdₑᵣ = 2π r h = 2π (1)(20) = 40π cm² 

The Area of the Circular Ends

 Aₑₙdₛ = 2 × π r² = 2 × π (1)² = 2π cm²

Total Surface Area of the Hollowed-out Ball

 Aₕₒₗₗₒwₑd = Aₛₚₕₑᵣₑ + A꜀yₗᵢₙdₑᵣ - Aₑₙdₛ

Substituting the values:

 Aₕₒₗₗₒwₑd = 400π + 40π - 2π = 438π cm² 

Ratio of the Total Surface Area of the Hollowed-out Ball to the Surface Area of the Original Ball**:**

**= frac{A{ₕₒₗₗₒwₑd}}{A{ₛₚₕₑᵣₑ}} = (438π)/(400π) = (438)/(400) = (219)/(200)**

**The ratio of the total surface area of the hollowed-out ball to the surface area of the original ball is (219)/(200).**

questions.question: If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same work in 2 days, then the time taken by 10 men and 20 boys for doing the same piece of work will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

6 men and 8 boys can complete the work in 10 days.

26 men and 48 boys can complete the work in 2 days.

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

Let the efficiency of one man = M and one boy = B.

Total work = (Efficiency of 6 men and 8 boys) × 10 = (Efficiency of 26 men and 48 boys) × 2.

**Calculation:**

Calculate the total work in terms of M and B:

From the first case:

Work = (6M + 8B) × 10 = 60M + 80B.

From the second case:

Work = (26M + 48B) × 2 = 52M + 96B.

Equating the work:

60M + 80B = 52M + 96B

8M = 16B

M = 2B

Calculate the time taken by 10 men and 20 boys:

Efficiency of 10 men and 20 boys:

Total efficiency = 10M + 20B

= 10(2B) + 20B = 20B + 20B = 40B.

From the first case, total work = 60M + 80B = 60(2B) + 80B = 120B + 80B = 200B.

Time taken = Total work ÷ Total efficiency

= 200B ÷ 40B = 5 days.

**∴ The time taken by 10 men and 20 boys to complete the work is 5 days.**

questions.question: The diagonal and one side of a rectangular plot are 65 m and 63 m, respectively. What is the perimeter of the rectangular plot?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diagonal of the rectangular plot = 65 m

One side of the rectangular plot = 63 m

**Formula Used:**

Using the Pythagorean theorem for the right-angled triangle formed by the diagonal and sides of the rectangle.

Diagonal² = Length² + Breadth²

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

**Calculation:**

Let the length be 63 m and the breadth be b meters.

Using the Pythagorean theorem:

Diagonal² = Length² + Breadth²

65² = 63² + b²

4225 = 3969 + b²

⇒ b² = 4225 - 3969

⇒ b² = 256

⇒ b = 16 m

Perimeter of the rectangular plot = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (63 + 16) = 2 × 79 = 158 m

**The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: The smallest natural number that must be added to 1212 to make it a perfect square is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number to be made a perfect square = 1212

**Formula Used:**

For a number n that is not a perfect square, the smallest natural number to be added to make it a perfect square is the difference between the next perfect square greater than and n .

**Calculation:**

Find the next perfect square greater than 1212.

√1212 ≈ 34.8

The next integer after 34.8 is 35.

Next perfect square = 35²

35² = 1225

Smallest natural number to be added = 1225 - 1212

Smallest natural number = 13

**The smallest natural number that must be added to 1212 to make it a perfect square is 13.**

questions.question: A sum of money, on compound interest, amounts to ₹5,290 in 2 years and to ₹6,083.50 in 3 years. If interest is compounded annually, then the rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of money after 2 years = ₹5,290

The sum of money after 3 years = ₹6,083.50

Interest is compounded annually.

**Formula Used:**

Amount after n years = P(1 + r)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P and the rate of interest per annum be r.

From the given data:

P(1 + r)² = 5,290

P(1 + r)³ = 6,083.50

Dividing both equations:

 (P(1 + r)³)/(P(1 + r)²) = (6,083.50)/(5,290) 

⇒ (1 + r) = 6,083.50 / 5,290

⇒ 1 + r = 1.15

⇒ r = 0.15 = 15%

**The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: A 250 m long train running at a speed of 100 km/h crosses another train, coming from the opposite direction at a speed of 62 km/h, in 10 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of first train = 250 m

Speed of first train = 100 km/h

Speed of second train = 62 km/h

Time to cross each other = 10 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (when moving in opposite direction) = Speed of first train + Speed of second train

Distance = Relative speed × Time

Total Distance = Length of first train + Length of second train

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 100 km/h + 62 km/h

Relative speed = 162 km/h = 162 × (5/18) m/s = 45 m/s

Time = 10 seconds

Distance covered in 10 seconds = 45 m/s × 10 s = 450 m

Total Distance = Length of first train + Length of second train

450 m = 250 m + Length of second train

⇒ Length of second train = 450 m - 250 m = 200 m

**The length of the second train is 200 m.**

questions.question: If the mean of 22, 25, 27, 24 and x is 26, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 22, 25, 27, 24, and x

Mean = 26

**Formula Used:**

Mean = (Sum of all values) / (Number of values)

**Calculation:**

Number of values = 5

Sum of all values = 22 + 25 + 27 + 24 + x

⇒ 26 = (22 + 25 + 27 + 24 + x) / 5

⇒ 26 × 5 = 98 + x

⇒ 130 = 98 + x

⇒ x = 32

**The value of x is 32.**
